title: Centers adapted to labelled normal-crossings coordinates
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf and $(W_j)_{j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}}$ a finite family of quasi-coherent ideals [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Say that the center $V(I)$ has adapted normal-crossings coordinates for this labelled family if at each $x\in V(I)$ there are an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $x$, integers $s,m,n\geq0$ with $m\leq s$, sections $z_1,\ldots,z_s,y_1,\ldots,y_n$ on $U$, an injection $\lambda:\{1,\ldots,s\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and a regular system of parameters $t$ of the Noetherian local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], such that the germs of the list $(z_1,\ldots,z_s,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ form a sublist of $t$, the image of $\lambda$ consists exactly of the indices of components through $x$, $W_{\lambda(k)}(U)=(z_k)$, $W_j(U)=(1)$ for indices outside that image, and $I(U)=(z_1,\ldots,z_m,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$. The condition is imposed only along $V(I)$, and the empty center sequence $m=n=0$ is permitted.
